checks.name: counting-rule
checks.summary: The counting rule, implemented as dp-v2-087 d2 states it and documented in internal/store/memory/store.go's own comments with the Firestore line each clause mirrors. What is counted is the set of distinct RECORD KEYS a transaction touched, namespaced by KIND (the Firestore collection name), so two aggregates sharing an id are two records exactly as they are two document paths. (a) a key counts once per transaction however many times it is read, mirroring u.cache being keyed by document path; (b) a MISS counts as one read, mirroring firestore/store.go:499-513 caching nil for a NotFound; (c) a paged read counts min(limit+1, rows remaining after the cursor) through the boundedWindow helper, because the Firestore query is Limit(limit+1) and countReads sees every snapshot returned -- PendingControlProgresses is the single bounded query whose Firestore form is Limit(limit) with no probe row, and it is charged without the +1 accordingly; (d) the quota record counts as one read and one write; (e) a write counts its key once, mirroring len(u.values); (f) a single-key read of a key already written in the same transaction counts NOTHING (countKeyedRead short-circuits on the write set, mirroring u.value), while the paths where Firestore reaches the server anyway -- read() and every query -- go through countFetchedReads, which deliberately does not short-circuit; (g) deletes stay zero, because neither adapter has a delete operation. Three mirrors were needed beyond the obvious ones, and each is what makes A6's rows agree: adjustCounter's sharded queue-counter document is charged one read and one write per aggregate status change, with the same crc32.ChecksumIEEE(id) modulo 32 shard the Firestore adapter uses, even though this adapter keeps no counter record; QueueSummary is charged all 32 counter documents, because the Firestore counterpart batch-gets them all; and the Provider registry is charged as ONE document per Provider name, because that is where the Firestore adapter keeps the observation ring and the assignment index that this adapter splits across three maps. The true-up runs inside Store.Transact AFTER the callback returns nil and BEFORE m.data = working, so it applies to the CLONE: a failed transaction drops the reservation and the correction together, which is the same rollback semantics an aborted Firestore transaction has. quota.Counter.TrueUp is REUSED, not reimplemented, and internal/quota is byte-unchanged.

checks.name: outcome-asserted-with-committed-totals
checks.summary: The outcome asserted directly, in internal/store/memory/store_test.go's TestManyReadTransactionsFitInOneDayOnTheInMemoryAdapter, on ONE fixed injected instant, with the committed total asserted and not merely the absence of an error. Three sub-assertions, all green: (1) `a handful of read transactions costs a fraction of the day`: the five read transactions whose fifth used to be refused now all succeed, and the COMMITTED daily total afterwards is exactly {Reads:20 Writes:5 Deletes:0} -- five times the measured per-transaction cost of {Reads:4 Writes:1} -- which is 0.08 per cent of quota.DefaultBudget.Reads; the test fails unless total reads times 100 is below the budget. (2) `every read transaction the settled arithmetic admits succeeds`: the bound is DERIVED, not chosen -- (quota.DefaultBudget.Reads - quota.ReadTransactionUsage.Reads) / measured-cost + 1 = (25000 - 6001) / 4 + 1 = 4750 read transactions, all of which succeed. The COMMITTED TOTAL afterwards is asserted exactly: {Reads:19000 Writes:4750 Deletes:0}, which is 4750 times the measured per-transaction cost and is below the budget. It is not the round 25000/4 = 6250, because the worst case is STILL reserved before each transaction and 6250 would not fit -- which is the point: the very next transaction, number 4751, is asserted to be refused with quota.ErrOverBudget. That refusal is what excludes a raised budget (non_goals item 1) and a reservation moved after the work or removed (non_goals item 2) at the same time; a settled reservation is the only thing that produces exactly this pair of numbers. (3) `mutations settle their reservation the same way`: the number of mutations that used to be a whole day's capacity, quota.DefaultBudget.Writes / quota.MutationUsage.Writes = 625, all succeed, and the committed total is asserted exactly at 625 times the measured single-capture cost of {Reads:4 Writes:5}, that is {Reads:2500 Writes:3125 Deletes:0}, against a write budget of 10000. One mutation settling to 5 writes against a worst case of 16 is asserted too, so a true-up that credits nothing back fails this test.
